_about: The GenSwarms landing page catalogue: every string the page shows or reads out, in English. Generated by `node website/build.mjs --extract`; do not edit.

To translate: write website/i18n/<file>.json (file: es, ko, zh, ru, tr) as a JSON object { "<id>": "<translation>", … } with every id below, plus "_same_as_english": [ids] for strings whose right translation is the English itself (they are checked, so list them deliberately). Keep your term decisions in website/i18n/<file>.ledger.md.

kind: meta = search and share snippets (plain text); html = the inner HTML of one element (keep every tag exactly, same attributes;   is a non-breaking space you may keep, move or drop); attr = an accessible name or tooltip (plain text, no tags); svg = a label drawn inside a figure (plain text, short); js = the suggestion bar, shown to readers whose browser prefers your language; 404 = the not-found page.
placeholders: {n}, {title}, {cap} are filled in by the page. Keep each exactly once, in the place your grammar needs.

max (svg labels): about how many Latin or Cyrillic characters fit on one line; count each Chinese or Korean character as two. lines: how many lines the label may wrap to (1 = it must fit on one line; a longer one is set smaller). Stay within it: the build fits what it can, and the layout audit fails on labels that overlap.
limit: a hard limit in characters; chars for most languages, cjk for Chinese and Korean. The build refuses longer text.

Protected names (_protect) must appear verbatim in your translation whenever the English has them. Names in the keep list (product, company and language names, file names, and the identifiers drawn in the figures such as telegram, triage, message_routed, swarm.state) are not in the catalogue: they stay as they are.

Constraints (playbook §8): translate by meaning, not word by word; do not make text longer than the English (it has to fit the layout); do not strengthen claims; use the same term for the same concept everywhere.
